cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved a trial of this cheap coffee substitute. You may take the first sip before I fill my cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we just use the proper coffee? There's plenty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Reserve use is not approved until the trial fails. You may help us establish whether this saves money.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you replace my breakfast when it tastes awful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Compensation is approved: one croissant for one failed sip. You may begin; my cup remains empty until your verdict.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 withholds normal coffee permission pending the trial; A5 approves B compensation terms while keeping A cup unfilled until B verdict.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 usable alternative causes A3 reserve condition; B4 breakfast compensation demand causes A5 a specific one-sip bargain.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a practical alternative and B4 negotiates compensation rather than merely refusing, shaping the test terms.

heightening.evidence: B4 conditional cooperation makes A5 formalize limited exposure and a remedy while preserving B first trial.

specificity.evidence: A1 cheap substitute and empty cup, B2 proper coffee and B4 breakfast concern establish what is risked.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 one-croissant-for-one-sip tariff is earned by B4 actual condition and A status as approving tester.
